text:
incidents-bot: Paging on-call: observed sustained p99 > 5s for streaming /v1/generate in us-west-2. Impact: streaming stalls and increased tail latency for customers on tiered plan. Pager: https://redwood.inc/ops/3250004321 :rotating_light:

maya: saw alert, jumping in. any known deploys?

omar_oncall: I'm oncall, joining. can someone paste p95/p99 numbers and a short timeseries?

ash-sre: (sorry, ash here) grabbing metrics. current window 16:12–16:20 UTC:
- p50: 120ms
- p95: 760ms
- p99: 5.3s
- streaming stall rate (clients observing >1s chunk gap): 8.2%
- queue length for preproc workers: 42 (baseline 4)

ash-sre: graph link: https://graphs.redwood/internal/streaming/3250004321

lee-tokenizer: seeing backlog on tokenizer workers. Tokenize time spiked, per-request tokenize_ms now ~1.2s for some requests. Root cause candidate: prompt expansion growth from tool-schema ingestion.

rebecca-support: we shipped a config change this morning that turned on `json_mode: fast-embed` for a subset of accounts to improve parsing. I rolled it out at 09:04 PT. I can roll back immediately if needed.

nina-ml: if json_mode triggers full tool schema inlining per request, that would multiply tokens. Quick check: median prompt tokens for streaming requests jumped from ~280 to ~1.9k after rollout. That explains tokenizer CPU and KV cache pressure.

chris-customer: we're seeing streaming stalls in production, customers pinging support. need ETA/impact statement we can send.

omar_oncall: ok, priority: (1) reduce immediate customer impact (2) stop cascade causing p99 breach (3) root cause and postmortem. Proposed short mitigations: rollback json_mode flag for rollout cohort, enable prefix/KV cache for large templates, and route streaming requests to fallback model until preproc stabilizes. Thoughts?

lee-tokenizer: rollback json_mode should help quickly. also, the tokenizer process queue length shows GC spikes due to big string parsing. We can add a temporary hard cap on expansion size (e.g., max_template_expansion_tokens=800) to prevent 10x growth.

rebecca-support: rolling back now for the affected cohort. Status: 16:15 UTC rollback started.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by rebecca-support: rollback-config json_mode -> false (cohort: early-access). CI: green. Rolling out to 25% -> 100% in 3min.

ash-sre: after rollback beginning: queue length dropping from 42 -> 18 (observed at 16:18 UTC). p99 trending down to 3.1s. still elevated but improving.

nina-ml: additional quick mitigation: enable KV/prefix caching for the template namespace `templates/v2/*` and enable dedup of repeated tool schemas. I can flip caching now.

maya: please confirm impact window we communicate. chris, can you draft a short customer note? Need to be factual: partial rollback and ongoing mitigation.

chris-customer: draft: "We observed higher-than-normal streaming latency affecting a subset of requests in us-west-2. We rolled back a config change that caused prompt expansion and are seeing improvements; we continue to monitor and will follow up." Will send after you review.

ash-sre: at 16:22 UTC: p95 = 420ms, p99 = 1.1s, streaming stall rate = 1.5%. Queue length = 6. Looks stable so far.

lee-tokenizer: root cause notes for postmortem: a support-led config enabled full tool schema inlining at request time. This caused per-request token expansion and KV cache churn. Secondary effect: streaming chunking logic expects steady tokenizer perf; when tokenizer latched, chunk emission stalled.

omar_oncall: action items (short):
- rebecca-support: confirm rollout fully reverted and add guardrail in release pipeline to require perf run for inline schema flags (owner: rebecca, ETA: today EOD)
- lee-tokenizer: add runtime limit on expansion tokens + circuit-breaker for preproc queue (owner: lee, ETA: 6hrs)
- nina-ml: enable template namespace prefix caching + dedupe (owner: nina, ETA: 30min)
- ash-sre: monitor p99 and set automatic temporary rate-limit at 10% for heavy streaming clients if p99 > 2s for 3m (owner: ash, ETA: 15min)
- chris-customer & maya: outbound customer note (owner: chris, ETA: 30min)

rebecca-support: confirmed: rollback completed at 16:19 UTC. I'll open a PR to add the perf gate and label the config with `dangerous-expansion=true` so it can't be toggled without signoff.

deploy-bot: routing change: temporary fallback to smaller streaming model (redwood-mini) for cohort: early-access and for requests where template_size > 1200 tokens. Rollout started at 16:21 UTC.

ash-sre: monitoring: 16:28 UTC p95=210ms p99=480ms streaming stall rate=0.6% queue length=3. Looks normal. Marking incident as "mitigating".

maya: good job team. we'll keep this thread as the single source-of-truth. please update when owners close their action items. I'll kick off a postmortem once stable.

lee-tokenizer: quick note for postmortem writeup: include a small reproduction script showing template -> expanded size and tokenization timeline, and suggestions: precompute tool schemas, lazy inlining, or move schema fetch off the hot path.

chris-customer: sent customer note at 16:35 UTC. link: https://support.redwood/ticket/5231

omar_oncall: incident status: MITIGATING. next update planned in 45 minutes or on regression. Thanks all. :slightly_smiling_face:
